summary: Round 1 review of a documentation chore. The spec states the rule and its placement, but the round count, the wrong-result exception, and the Round limit boundary lack decidable definitions. One Blocker and three Major findings need author resolution before Green writes the contract text.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] spec.md FR-1: The round count leaves two cases undecided: parallel Review A/B/C results, and a first adversarial run after review rounds. Rationale: The spec calls the first audit result round 1. It adds a round for a re-review or adversarial rerun only. It never says that A/B/C share one round. It never says that a first adversarial pass adds one. The 'after the second round' trigger changes with the reading. The plan leaves the choice to Green.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Major] spec.md FR-2: Comprehension gap: The exception 'can hide a wrong result in the delivered work' has no decidable test. Rationale: The spec gives two examples but no rule that separates delivered-work errors from test tooling. The exception is the only path to a fix round after round two. Different orchestrators can classify the same finding differently.

F3 [Major] spec.md FR-3: The fit does not say which rule wins when an FR-2 fix round would be the third remediation round. Rationale: FR-2 grants one fix round. Round limit forbids a third round without the metadata escalation key. FR-3 only says the fix round counts toward the Round limit count. The boundary needs a stated outcome before Green writes the text.

F4 [Major] plan.md Task 1.1: The plan claims every Red case fails, but it does not require each case to search only new text. Rationale: 'Round limit', 'base track', and 're-review' already appear in contracts.md. A case matching those strings passes at Red. The failing-first proof then breaks.

F5 [Nit] spec.md FR-4: The phrase 'the phase's plan.md' can name a per-phase plan file, but the repo holds one plan.md per track. Rationale: The record-line form is exact. Only the file phrase needs a target such as the track plan under the current phase.

The Round limit counts remediation rounds per base track with an escalation key for a third round; the stop rule counts review and adversarial rounds per phase; the two counters differ and the boundary is not stated.
FR-1 says the first audit result is round 1 and each re-review or adversarial rerun adds one. A first adversarial pass after review rounds is not a rerun, so its round number is undefined.
FR-2 gives the gate-script and wrong-dashboard-number examples but no general test for the exception; FR-5 repeats the same two examples.
FR-5 Math D1 example matches the spec narrative at line 9: a fourth-round finding on the phase's own gate script goes to tech-debt.
FR-4 gives the exact record line '- Late finding <id>: <tech-debt|one-fix-round> (<reason>)' and places records in the phase plan.md; the repo holds one plan.md per track.

No live copy of the rule text needs an update: 'Round limit' appears only in contracts.md, the archive, the 2026-11-10 review, and this track. claude-skills/ and skills/measure-orchestrator-workspace/ have no match. claude-skills/measure.skill is an April 2026 zip of the base measure skill with no orchestrator contracts.

paraphrase.proposes: This track documents a stop rule for late findings in the measure-orchestrator skill. After the second review or adversarial round of a phase, a new finding goes to measure/tech-debt.md instead of Green. A finding that can hide a wrong result in the delivered work gets one fix round. The orchestrator records each call and its reason in the phase plan. The rule text, a record-line form, a two-rule fit, and an example go in contracts.md, with pointer lines in SKILL.md and four role files.
paraphrase.current_system: Per the spec, contracts.md holds the Re-review scope rule and the Round limit rule. Re-review scope keeps a kept routed finding and a defect in changed lines blocking, and treats other new findings as nonblocking. Round limit sends open findings to the user after the second remediation round for a base track, with an escalation key escape hatch for a third round. SKILL.md points to contracts.md under its Contracts section. The four named role files hold only re-review CONTEST handling and no round logic.
